offer_letter.markdown:
# Offer of employment — Branch Manager (Channel Manager: Sales and Service)

## 1. Job Offer: Branch Manager (Channel Manager: Sales and Service)

Dear {{employee.full_name}},

We are happy to offer you the role of Branch Manager, also called Channel Manager: Sales and Service, at Absa Group. You will lead branch operations, manage teams, grow sales and service, oversee DHA and MVNO functions, and build a strong, compliant, customer-focused branch. You will also carry out other duties that fit this role when we reasonably ask you to.

## 2. Start Date and Work Location

Your job starts on 1 December 2026. This is a permanent position. You will work from Barberton, head office. The first 3 months are a probation period. During this time, we will check your performance and give you guidance and support.

## 3. Hours and Pay

You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, 5 days a week, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60-minute meal break after no more than 5 hours of work. We will pay you R18,000.00 a month as your basic salary. This works out to R103.85 per hour. We pay by EFT on the 25th of each month. We deduct PAYE and 1% UIF from your pay as required by law.

## 4. Leave and Other Terms

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave each year. You also get sick leave, family responsibility leave, maternity leave, and parental leave as set out in your contract. Your full terms, including notice periods and confidentiality duties, are in the attached employment contract.

## 5. Next Steps

Please send us your ID and qualifications so we can finish your onboarding. This offer is open until 30 November 2026. If you have questions, contact us at hr@example.co.za.

## 6. Acceptance

Please sign and date this letter to accept the offer: {{employee.full_name}}, {{date_signed}}.

contract.markdown:
# Contract of employment — Branch Manager (Channel Manager: Sales and Service)

## 1. Parties

This contract of employment is entered into between Absa Group, of 1 Main Road, Barberton (the Employer), and {{employee.full_name}}, identity number {{employee.id_number}}, of {{employee.address}} (the Employee).

## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Branch Manager (Channel Manager: Sales and Service). The Employee's duties include: Lead nodal operations with accountability for people, process, and performance.; Drive commercial growth and service excellence across multiple (SSO’s); Oversee DHA, MVNO functions, ensuring efficient verification and ID smart card issuing.; Strengthen compliance and operational integrity in civic services.; Inspire and empower teams to deliver exceptional customer experiences.; Expand market presence through oversight of RIB and External sales.; Harness technology to optimize efficiency and innovation.; Build resilient, high-performing teams aligned to strategic goals.; Ensure delivery of all performance targets with commercial focus.; Champion operational leadership that advances Africa’s service landscape.; Translate regional and national strategy into branch execution; Drive transformation, digital adoption, and inclusion initiatives; Position the branch as a trusted financial partner in the community; Full Branch P&L accountability (where applicable); Deliver growth, profitability, and productivity targets; Optimise multi-channel and integrated service models; Lead senior branch leadership and management teams; Build a leadership pipeline and succession plans; Foster ethical leadership, engagement, and accountability; Overall accountability for branch risk, conduct, and regulatory compliance; Manage audits, governance forums, and material risk events; Ensure strong control environments and TCF adherence; Engage key clients, community structures, and external partners; Act as a brand ambassador for the bank; Deliver a consistently exceptional in-branch customer experience by proactively welcoming, guiding, and supporting customers; Promote efficient service, alternative banking channels; Upholding Absa’s service standards, image, and brand in a safe, professional, and well‑managed branch environment. The Employer may reasonably require the Employee to perform other duties consistent with the position.

## 3. Commencement

Employment commences on 1 December 2026 on a permanent basis.

## 4. Probation

The first 3 month(s) of employment are a probationary period during which the Employer will assess the Employee's performance against the requirements of the position and give reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. Confirmation, extension or termination at the end of probation will follow a fair procedure.

## 5. Place of work

The Employee's place of work is Barberton, head office.

## 6. Hours of work

The Employee's ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days per week (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00). A meal interval of 60 minutes is taken after no more than five hours of continuous work. The Employee is entitled to a daily rest period of at least 12 consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours.

## 7. Remuneration

The Employee will be paid R18,000.00 per month (basic salary), equivalent to R103.85 per ordinary hour, payable monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments are payable. No payments in kind are made.

## 8. Overtime

Overtime is worked only by agreement and may not exceed ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the Employee's ordinary hourly wage, or, by agreement, compensated with paid time off. Work on a Sunday is paid at double the ordinary wage (or one and a half times if the Employee ordinarily works on Sundays), and work on a public holiday at double the ordinary wage.

## 9. Deductions

The following deductions will be made from the Employee's remuneration: PAYE; UIF 1%. No other deduction will be made without the Employee's written agreement in respect of a specific debt, or as required by law, a court order or an arbitration award.

## 10. Leave

The Employee is entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave per annual leave cycle of 12 months, to be taken at a time agreed with the Employer and not later than six months after the end of the cycle. Sick leave: 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle (during the first six months, one day for every 26 days worked); a medical certificate may be required for absences of more than two consecutive days or on more than two occasions in eight weeks. Maternity leave: at least 4 consecutive months. Parental leave: 10 consecutive days. Adoption and commissioning parental leave as provided in the Act. Family responsibility leave: 3 days' paid leave per year once employed for longer than four months and for at least four days a week.

## 11. Termination and notice

Either party may terminate this contract on written notice of one week if the employee has been employed for six months or less; two weeks if employed for more than six months but not more than one year; four weeks if employed for more than one year. Notice may not be given during any period of leave. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from terminating employment summarily for a fair reason following a fair procedure, or the parties from agreeing to waive notice.

## 12. Bargaining council or sectoral determination

No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to the Employer's business.

## 13. Confidentiality

The Employee will not, during or after employment, disclose or use any confidential information of the Employer, its clients or suppliers, except as required to perform the Employee's duties or by law.

## 14. Other documents

No other documents form part of this contract.

## 15. General

This contract records the whole agreement between the parties on its subject; any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties. Where any term is less favourable to the Employee than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the more favourable provision applies. The Employer will keep these particulars for three years after termination and will explain them to the Employee on request.

## 16. Signatures

Signed at ____________ on {{date_signed}}.

For the Employer: {{employer.signatory}}  ____________________

The Employee: {{employee.full_name}}  ____________________

plain_language.explanation: This clause names who is making the agreement: Absa Group, based at 1 Main Road, Barberton, and you as the employee. It records your ID number and address so the contract is tied to you specifically.

You are being hired as Branch Manager, also known as Channel Manager: Sales and Service. This clause lists your main duties, covering leadership, sales growth, compliance, customer service, and team building. Your employer can also ask you to do other reasonable tasks that fit this role.
Your job starts on 1 December 2026. It is a permanent position, meaning there is no fixed end date.

Your first 3 months are a trial period where your employer checks if you are doing the job well. You will get fair guidance, training, and feedback during this time. Any decision to confirm, extend, or end your job after probation must follow a fair process.
You will work at the Barberton head office.

You will work 40 hours a week, spread over 5 days, 8 hours a day, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60-minute meal break after working no more than 5 hours straight. You are also entitled to at least 12 hours of rest between workdays and at least 36 hours of rest each week.

You earn R18,000.00 each month as your basic salary, which equals R103.85 per hour. This is paid on the 25th of each month by EFT. You will not receive any extra cash payments or payments in goods or services.

You only work overtime if you agree to it, and it cannot go over 10 hours in a week. Overtime pay is 1.5 times your normal hourly rate, or you can agree to take paid time off instead. If you work on a Sunday, you get double pay (or 1.5 times if Sundays are part of your normal schedule), and public holiday work is always paid at double your normal rate.

Your employer will deduct PAYE (income tax) and 1% for UIF from your salary. No other money will be taken from your pay unless you agree to it in writing, or the law, a court, or an arbitration award requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave each year, which you must use within 6 months after the leave year ends, at a time agreed with your employer. You get 30 days of paid sick leave every 3 years, though in your first 6 months you earn 1 day of sick leave for every 26 days worked; your employer may ask for a doctor's note if you are off for more than 2 days in a row or more than twice in 8 weeks. You also get at least 4 months of maternity leave, 10 days of parental leave, and the adoption leave the law provides. After 4 months of employment, if you work at least 4 days a week, you get 3 days of paid family responsibility leave per year.

Either you or your employer can end the contract by giving written notice. The notice period is 1 week if you have worked 6 months or less, 2 weeks if you have worked between 6 months and 1 year, and 4 weeks if you have worked more than 1 year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. Your employer can still dismiss you immediately for a fair reason if a fair process is followed, and both sides can agree to skip the notice period.
No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to your employer's business, so these rules do not affect your contract.

You must keep the Employer's, its clients', and its suppliers' confidential information private, both while working there and after you leave. You may only share this information if it's needed to do your job or if the law requires it.
No other documents besides this contract form part of your agreement with the Employer.

This contract is the complete agreement between you and your employer, and any changes must be written and signed by both of you. If any part of this contract gives you less than what the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, a sectoral determination, or a collective agreement requires, the better terms will apply instead. Your employer will keep your employment records for 3 years after you leave and will explain any terms to you if you ask.
This section is where both parties sign the contract. The Employer's signatory signs on behalf of Absa Group, and you, the Employee, sign to confirm you agree to the terms, with the date filled in.
